lines.text: Is your Brita actually cleaning your water or just making it taste better?
ai: a water filter pitcher pouring crystal clear water into a glass

lines.text: His tap water reads 259 parts per million of dissolved stuff.
ai: tiny glowing particles floating in a glass of tap water macro

lines.text: Then he builds a filter from a plastic bottle with sand and carbon for five bucks and it drops to 237.
ai: a homemade plastic bottle filter with layers of sand and black charcoal

lines.text: And the 28 dollar Brita lands at 234 which is basically the same as the five dollar bottle.
ai: a water filter pitcher next to a plastic bottle filter on a kitchen counter
two glasses of water side by side under a spotlight

lines.text: That's because a Brita is mostly activated carbon which grabs chlorine and bad taste but lets dissolved minerals slide right through.
ai: macro of black activated carbon granules with water flowing through
tiny minerals sliding through charcoal macro

lines.text: And the 300 dollar Berkey reads higher than tap water at 284 although that's common when the filters are brand new.
ai: a tall stainless steel water filter tank in a kitchen
brand new water filter cartridges in a box

lines.text: But the 29 dollar ZeroWater hits zero.
ai: a perfectly clear glass of water with a glowing light behind it

lines.text: Because it uses ion exchange beads that swap every dissolved mineral for the ingredients of pure water.
ai: macro of tiny amber resin beads with water flowing over them
glowing beads swapping particles in water macro

lines.text: But a high number doesn't mean your water is unsafe because a lot of it is just calcium and magnesium.
ai: white calcium crystals in a glass of water macro
a calm glass of mineral water on a stone table

lines.text: So what does your water read?
ai: a water filter pitcher pouring crystal clear water into a glass
